prompt: If one wanted to create a data quality application that runs on data stored in HDFS, what would be a good way to approach this? Specifically, assuming the user has defined data quality rules, what would be a good way to evaluate them (specifically in terms of performance)?
response: To create a data quality application on HDFS, you can use MapReduce to process the data. Storing the data quality rules in a separate file and reading them during runtime is a good approach. For performance, you can cache the rules in memory if they are large. This way, you can efficiently evaluate the data against the rules.
